intro.objective: Recognise a quadratic sequence by its constant second difference, and find the nth term in the form an² + bn + c using the second-difference method.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to HALVE the second difference to find a (the coefficient of n²).
Making arithmetic slips when subtracting the an² values from the sequence.
Not finding the leftover linear part (bn + c) correctly.
Sign errors, especially when the linear part is negative.
methodSteps: Step 1: Find the first differences between consecutive terms.
Step 2: Find the second differences — for a quadratic these are constant.
Step 3: a = second difference ÷ 2; this gives the an² part.
Step 4: Subtract an² from each term to leave a linear sequence; find its nth term (bn + c).
Step 5: Combine to get an² + bn + c and check by substituting n = 1, 2.
workedExample: Step 3 — a = 2 ÷ 2 = 1, so the n² part is n².

frame: First differences are the gaps between terms; second differences are the gaps between those.
questions.content:
Find the first and second differences of each sequence.

   a) 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, …
   b) 4, 7, 12, 19, 28, …

frame: A sequence is quadratic if its SECOND differences are constant.
questions.content:
State whether each sequence is quadratic. Show the second differences.

   a) 1, 4, 9, 16, …
   b) 2, 4, 6, 8, …

Find the nth term of each quadratic sequence.

   a) 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, …
   b) 4, 7, 12, 19, 28, …
   c) 3, 9, 19, 33, 51, …

A sequence has nth term n² + n.

   a) Find the 1st term.
   b) Find the 5th term.
   c) Find the 10th term.

Find the nth term of each quadratic sequence.

   a) 0, 3, 8, 15, 24, …
   b) 5, 14, 27, 44, 65, …
   c) 3, 8, 15, 24, …

A growing pattern of squares uses 2, 6, 12, 20, … tiles for patterns 1, 2, 3, 4.

   a) How many tiles are in pattern 5? (1 mark)
   b) Find the nth term for the number of tiles. (2 marks)

A quadratic sequence is 1, 6, 15, 28, 45, …

   a) Show that the second difference is constant. (1 mark)
   b) Find the nth term. (2 marks)
   c) Find the 10th term. (1 mark)

A quadratic sequence has nth term n² − 3n + 2.

   a) Find the first four terms. (2 marks)
   b) Show that the second difference is 2. (1 mark)
   c) Which term has the value 30? (2 marks)

answers.title: Teacher key
rows: Q1: a) first 3, 5, 7, 9; second 2, 2, 2  b) first 3, 5, 7, 9; second 2, 2, 2
Q2: a) second differences 2, 2 → quadratic  b) first differences all 2, second differences 0 → not quadratic (it is linear)
Q3: a) a = 1 → n²; subtract gives 1, 1, 1… → n² + 1  b) n² + 3  c) second difference 4 → a = 2 (2n²); subtract gives 1,1,1… → 2n² + 1
Q5: a) n² − 1  b) second difference 4 → a = 2; subtract 2n² gives 3, 6, 9… = 3n → 2n² + 3n  c) n² + 2n
Q6: a) 30 tiles  b) second difference 2 → a = 1 (n²); subtract gives 1, 2, 3, 4 = n → n² + n
Q7: a) first differences 5, 9, 13, 17; second differences 4, 4, 4 (constant)  b) a = 2 (2n²); subtract gives −1, −2, −3… = −n → 2n² − n  c) 2(100) − 10 = 190
Q8: a) 0, 0, 2, 6  b) first differences 0, 2, 4; second differences 2, 2  c) n² − 3n + 2 = 30 → n² − 3n − 28 = 0 → (n − 7)(n + 4) = 0 → n = 7 (the 7th term)
